questions.q: Direct: "I am tired." Reported: She said she ___ tired.
questions.why: Present simple backshifts to past simple when the reporting verb is in the past.

questions.q: Direct: "I work in a bank." He told me he ___ in a bank.
questions.why: Present simple 'work' becomes past simple 'worked' after a past reporting verb.

questions.q: Direct: "We are leaving now." They said they ___ leaving then.
questions.why: Present continuous 'are leaving' backshifts to past continuous 'were leaving'.

questions.q: Direct: "I have finished." He said he ___ finished.
questions.why: Present perfect 'have finished' backshifts to past perfect 'had finished'.

questions.q: Direct: "I saw her yesterday." He said he ___ her the day before.
questions.why: Past simple usually backshifts to past perfect in reported speech.

questions.q: Direct: "I will call you." She said she ___ call me.
questions.why: 'Will' backshifts to 'would' after a past reporting verb.

questions.q: Direct: "I can swim." He said he ___ swim.
questions.why: The modal 'can' backshifts to 'could' in reported speech.

questions.q: Direct: "I may be late." She said she ___ be late.
questions.why: 'May' backshifts to 'might' when reporting a past statement.

questions.q: Direct: "The Earth is round." The teacher said the Earth ___ round.
questions.why: Backshift is optional for general truths or facts that are still true.

questions.q: Direct: "I live here now." He said he lived there ___.
questions.why: In reported speech 'now' usually changes to 'then'.

questions.q: Direct: "I'll do it tomorrow." She said she would do it ___.
questions.why: 'Tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' (or 'the following day') in reported speech.

questions.q: Direct: "I met him yesterday." He said he had met him ___.
questions.why: 'Yesterday' becomes 'the day before' (or 'the previous day') in reported speech.

questions.q: Direct: "Come here." She told me to come ___.
questions.why: The place word 'here' usually changes to 'there' in reported speech.

questions.q: Direct: "I bought this book." He said he had bought ___ book.
questions.why: The demonstrative 'this' changes to 'that' in reported speech.

questions.q: She said to me, "You look great." → She said ___ looked great.
questions.why: Pronouns shift to the speaker's viewpoint; 'you' (me) becomes 'I'.

questions.q: Tom said, "My sister called." → Tom said ___ sister had called.
questions.why: The possessive 'my' shifts to 'his' to match Tom's viewpoint.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: He ___ me that he was busy.
questions.why: 'Tell' is followed by a person object; you tell someone something.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: She ___ that the shop was closed.
questions.why: 'Say' is not followed by a person object; you say something (to someone).

questions.q: Direct: "Where do you live?" He asked me where I ___.
questions.why: Reported questions use statement word order with no auxiliary 'do'.

questions.q: Direct: "What are you doing?" She asked what I ___ doing.
questions.why: Reported questions keep statement order and backshift the verb.

questions.q: Direct: "Are you ready?" He asked ___ I was ready.
questions.why: Yes/no questions are reported with 'if' or 'whether'.

questions.q: Direct: "Do you like tea?" She asked me ___ I liked tea.
questions.why: Yes/no questions use 'if' or 'whether'; there is no question word.

questions.q: Which is correctly reported? Direct: "When does the train leave?"
options: He asked when does the train leave.
He asked when the train left.
He asked when did the train leave.
He asked when the train did leave.
questions.answer: He asked when the train left.
questions.why: Reported wh-questions use statement order and drop 'does/did'.

questions.q: Direct: "Close the door." She told me ___ the door.
questions.why: Reported commands use 'tell/ask someone + to + infinitive'.

questions.q: Direct: "Please help me." He asked me ___ him.
questions.why: Reported requests use 'ask someone + to + infinitive'.

questions.q: Direct: "Don't touch it." She told me ___ touch it.
questions.why: Negative commands are reported as 'told/asked someone not to + verb'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Direct: "I am hungry." → He said he ___ hungry.'
questions.why: Present simple 'am' backshifts to past simple 'was'.

questions.q: Type the answer with one word: 'She ___ me that she was leaving.' (tell/say)
questions.why: Use 'told' because there is a person object after the verb.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Direct: "Are you coming?" → He asked ___ I was coming.' (one word, not whether)
questions.why: Yes/no questions are reported with 'if' (or 'whether').

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Direct: "Sit down." → The teacher told us ___ ___ down.' (two words)
questions.why: Reported commands use 'tell someone to + base verb'.

questions.q: 'I'm tired,' he said. → He said he ___ tired.
questions.why: Present simple shifts back to past simple in reported speech.

questions.q: 'I'll help you,' she said. → She said she ___ help me.
questions.why: 'Will' becomes 'would' in reported speech.

questions.q: 'Where do you live?' → He asked me where I ___ .
questions.why: Reported questions: statement order + tense shift.

questions.q: 'Don't touch it!' → She told me ___ it.
questions.why: Negative reported commands: told + object + not to + verb.

questions.q: 'I saw the film yesterday.' → He said he had seen the film ___ .
questions.why: 'Yesterday' becomes 'the day before' in reported speech.
